title: Change Management Policy
text: Every change to a production system is classified as standard, normal, or emergency. Standard changes are pre-authorised, low-risk, and follow a documented procedure. Normal changes require review before release. Emergency changes may bypass pre-approval but must be retroactively documented and reviewed by the Change Advisory Board within two business days. Change records must capture the requester, the implementer, the reviewer, the rollback plan, and the verification evidence. A change implemented without a change record is a reportable control failure regardless of its outcome.

title: Production Change Control Standard for Regulated Systems
text: Production changes that touch personal data require Change Advisory Board approval and two independent reviewers before release. The reviewers must not include the author of the change. Segregation of duties applies: the person who approves a change to a regulated system may not be the person who deploys it. Evidence of approval must be linked to the deployment record and retained for seven years to satisfy audit sampling. Deployments to regulated systems are prohibited during the quarterly financial close window unless an emergency exception is granted by the compliance officer.

title: Data Processing and Lawful Basis Policy
text: Any new processing of personal data must be recorded in the processing register before processing begins, naming the controller, the purpose, the categories of data subjects, the lawful basis, and the retention period. Processing without a documented lawful basis is prohibited. Purpose limitation applies: data collected for one purpose may not be reused for a materially different purpose without a new lawful basis assessment. Data minimisation requires that each field in a processing workflow be justified by the stated purpose. Changes to the purpose, the categories of data, or the recipients require the register entry to be updated and re-reviewed by the data protection officer.

title: Data Retention and Deletion Policy
text: Retention periods are set by data category and are enforced by automated deletion jobs. Logs containing personal data must be purged within 30 days unless a legal hold applies. Customer transaction records are retained for seven years to meet statutory accounting obligations. Marketing consent records are retained for the life of the consent plus two years. Backups inherit the retention period of the data they contain, and a deletion request is not complete until it has propagated to backups within the documented backup cycle. Retention periods may not be extended informally; an extension requires a documented legal or regulatory basis.

title: Data Protection Impact Assessment Procedure
text: A data protection impact assessment is required before implementing a new data processing workflow that involves large-scale processing of special category data, systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area, automated decision-making with legal effect, or the combination of datasets from separate sources. The assessment documents the necessity and proportionality of the processing, the risks to data subjects, and the mitigations. It must be completed and signed off by the data protection officer before the workflow is deployed, not retrospectively. A material change to an assessed workflow triggers a reassessment.

title: Production Security Policy
text: Verbose request tracing must not be enabled in production environments because request and response payloads may contain credentials, authentication tokens, and personal data. Diagnostic mechanisms that capture payloads are permitted only in environments containing synthetic data. Where production diagnosis is unavoidable, engineers must use payload-redacting sampling with field-level masking approved by the security team, and the collection must be time-boxed and logged as a privileged action. Any capture of unredacted production payloads is a security incident and must be reported within twenty-four hours.

title: Access Control and Privileged Operations Standard
text: Access follows least privilege and is granted through role assignments, never to individual accounts directly. Standing production access is not granted to engineers; elevated access is requested just in time, is justified against a ticket, expires automatically after four hours, and is fully session-recorded. Privileged operations in regulated systems require a second approver. Access rights are recertified quarterly by the owning manager, and any account inactive for sixty days is disabled. Shared accounts are prohibited because they defeat attribution during an investigation.

title: Audit Evidence and Control Testing Policy
text: Controls are tested on a quarterly cycle and evidence must be reproducible by an independent reviewer without the control owner's assistance. Evidence must be timestamped, attributable to an identity, and stored in the evidence repository rather than in personal drives or chat threads. Screenshots are accepted only where no machine-readable export exists. A control exception must record the compensating control, the risk acceptance owner, and an expiry date; exceptions without an expiry date are treated as control failures. Sampling for deployment approvals is performed across the full population of production changes in the period.

title: Third-Party and Subprocessor Management Policy
text: Any third party that processes personal data on the organisation's behalf is a subprocessor and must be assessed before onboarding and reassessed annually. The assessment covers security posture, data location, subprocessor chain, breach notification commitments, and deletion guarantees on termination. A data processing agreement must be executed before any data is transferred. Transfers outside the approved jurisdictions require a documented transfer mechanism and a transfer impact assessment. The subprocessor register is published and customers are notified of additions with thirty days notice.

title: Security Incident and Breach Notification Procedure
text: A suspected personal data breach must be reported internally to the security team immediately and in no case later than one hour after detection. The security team performs a risk assessment to determine whether the breach is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects. Where that threshold is met, the supervisory authority must be notified within seventy-two hours of becoming aware of the breach. Affected data subjects are notified without undue delay where the risk is high. The breach register records every incident including those assessed as not notifiable, with the reasoning retained.

title: Data Classification Standard
text: Data is classified as public, internal, confidential, or restricted. Restricted covers special category personal data, payment credentials, and authentication secrets. Classification is assigned by the data owner at creation and is inherited by derived datasets, so an aggregate built from restricted inputs is restricted until a documented anonymisation technique is applied and validated. Pseudonymised data remains personal data because re-identification remains possible with the key. Restricted data may not be copied to developer workstations or to non-production environments under any circumstances.

title: Segregation of Duties Control Matrix
text: Incompatible duty pairs are enforced technically wherever possible and by detective review otherwise. A person may not both author and approve the same change to a regulated system. A person may not both approve a payment and execute it. A person may not both administer the identity provider and grant themselves application roles. Where team size makes separation impossible, a documented compensating control with independent after-the-fact review is required, reviewed quarterly, and recorded as a formal exception with an expiry date.

title: Encryption and Key Management Standard
text: Personal data must be encrypted in transit using current TLS versions with deprecated cipher suites disabled, and at rest using platform-managed envelope encryption. Keys are managed in the key management service, are never exported in plaintext, and are rotated annually or immediately on suspicion of compromise. Application-level encryption is additionally required for restricted fields so that database administrators cannot read them. Cryptographic algorithms are selected from the approved list only; custom cryptographic implementations are prohibited without a formal cryptographic review.

title: Compliance Training and Attestation Policy
text: All staff complete data protection and security awareness training within thirty days of joining and annually thereafter. Engineers with production access complete an additional secure development module covering injection, access control, and secrets handling. Completion rates are reported to the audit committee quarterly and a completion rate below ninety-five percent is escalated. Staff attest annually that they have read the acceptable use policy and the code of conduct. Failure to complete mandatory training within the grace period results in suspension of production access until completed.

title: Continuous Control Monitoring Standard
text: Preventive controls are supplemented by automated continuous monitoring that evaluates the live configuration against policy and raises a finding within fifteen minutes of a drift. Monitored checks include public storage buckets, unencrypted volumes, overly permissive network rules, accounts without multi-factor authentication, expired access exceptions, and deployments lacking a linked change record. Findings are assigned to the owning team with a remediation deadline based on severity: critical within twenty-four hours, high within seven days. Repeat findings on the same control within a quarter are escalated to the risk committee.

title: Data Residency and Cross-Border Transfer Policy
text: Personal data belonging to European data subjects is processed and stored within the European region by default. A data processing workflow that would move personal data to another region requires an approved transfer mechanism, a transfer impact assessment, and sign-off from the data protection officer before deployment. Regional pinning is enforced at the infrastructure layer, and deployments that would place a regulated workload in a non-approved region are blocked by policy as code. Support access from outside the approved region is permitted only through a session-recorded jump host with no local data download.
